title: Action
description: One action the agent decides. Written to the shared database by HappyRobot workflows; the simulator applies its effects on the world; the dashboard renders the action log. Actions with real_interaction produce an actual call, email, or SMS. evidence and reasoning are mandatory: they are the transparency the judges score.

actor.description: Entity id that executes the action. The verb must be in that entity's capabilities and the target zones inside its jurisdiction. The value system is a valid actor for system verbs (register_entity, update_entity).

verb.description: The action verb. Two disjoint families with different validation. World verbs are open scenario vocabulary executed by entities; the World API rejects a verb not present in the actor's capabilities, so the runtime menu comes from the entity registry, never from this schema. System verbs are a closed set implemented and enforced by the crisis kernel itself (actor must be system): register_entity (create a discovered entity from a signal; params holds the entity object), update_entity (revise entity attributes from runtime evidence: units lost, status unreachable, trust downgraded), set_tripwire (install a standing rule: a condition on incoming signals that triggers kernel-executed actions in milliseconds, without agent deliberation; the agent's main self-programming mechanism), clear_tripwire (retire a standing rule), schedule_check (emit a timer event later; params holds delay_min and a reminder note). Agents must never invent system verbs; the kernel validates params per system verb.

target_zones.description: Zone ids the action applies to. Must be inside the actor's jurisdiction.

params.description: Verb-specific parameters. For send_es_alert: the message text. For rescue: number of units. For register_entity: the full new entity object.

status.description: Lifecycle state. pending_approval: waits for a human on the dashboard (required when the actor's activation cost is high), with a timeout that auto-escalates. approved: cleared to execute. in_progress: execution started but the outcome is not known yet (a voice call ringing, a responder traveling); the agent PATCHes the final state later. executed: done, outcome recorded. rejected: denied by the human supervisor. failed: real-world execution error (call not answered); the agent must then escalate via escalation_to.

items.description: A typed reference: sig-* (an observed signal), act-* (a prior action whose outcome motivates this one, e.g. escalating after a failed call), evt-* (a timer or system event).

evidence.description: References that justify this action. Mandatory and never empty: every decision must be traceable to something that happened. Signals are the common case; actions triggered by an earlier action's failure cite that action, and actions triggered by a timer cite the event.

reasoning.description: One or two sentences of agent reasoning for this action, written for a human supervisor (Gauge trend rising plus 4 corroborating reports upstream). Shown verbatim on the dashboard.

real_interaction.description: The real-world contact this action produced, if any. Filled after execution as proof of real interaction (a track requirement).

stubbed.description: True when the kernel's interim executor simulated the contact because the real channel (HappyRobot voice/SMS) is not wired yet. The dashboard must show stubbed interactions differently.
